title: Characterizing Questioning Patterns and Student Engagement Through Contextual Analysis of Real-Time Classroom Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2609.38907v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Real-time classroom polling is now routine, yet the data it produces is usually read narrowly, as a correctness score or a headcount. Such readings say little about what a poll is doing within a lecture or how it shapes engagement. This is particularly relevant for short-response formats such as True/False, where the same question format can be used to test recall, check comprehension, or direct students' attention to a deliberately misleading statement. This study asks whether a poll's answer and instructional function can be determined by reading it against its lecture transcript, what cognitive levels of Bloom's taxonomy and instructional-function clusters the corpus contains, and how student engagement relates to answering correctly. translated_title: 通过情境化分析实时课堂互动来刻画提问模式与学生参与度
translated_abstract: 实时课堂投票如今已成为常态，但其产生的数据通常被狭隘地解读为正确率分数或人数统计。这类解读难以说明投票在讲座中究竟发挥了什么作用，以及它如何影响学生参与度。这对判断题等简短作答形式尤为重要，因为同一题型既可以用于测试记忆，也可以用于检查理解，或引导学生关注一个刻意设置的误导性陈述。本研究探讨以下问题：能否通过将投票题目与其所属讲座的文字记录进行对照阅读，来判定投票的答案及其教学功能；该语料库涵盖哪些布鲁姆认知分类学层级和教学功能聚类；以及学生参与度与答题正确与否之间存在何种关系。我们分析了一个自然情境下的语料库：在39天内共47场直播课堂，包含604道投票题和来自2,807名学习者的340,668条作答记录，其中大多数题目为判断题，并与时间对齐的讲座文字记录进行对照分析。
tldr: 该研究通过将课堂投票题目与时间对齐的讲座文字记录对照分析，揭示投票题的认知层级与教学功能，并刻画学生参与度和答题正确率之间的关系。
en_tdlr: This study characterizes questioning patterns by contextualizing classroom poll questions against time-aligned lecture transcripts, revealing their cognitive levels and instructional functions, and examines how student engagement relates to answering correctly.
